title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page closes the 'first part' of a manuscript whose surrounding pages work on the arithmetic of 1-forms and the Cartier operator. The underlying problem is the rank-one case of the p-curvature conjecture. Let ω be a closed 1-form on X/S, with S of finite type over Z. Suppose that for almost all closed points s, the form ω(s) satisfies C(ω)=ω, i.e. it is locally a logarithmic derivative; equivalently, the connection d+ω has p-curvature zero. Is ω then globally (up to rational multiple) a dlog?

The previous page translates this for X→S an abelian scheme, and more generally for X proper smooth via the Albanese. One passes to the dual abelian scheme A and its universal vector extension E, which is the moduli of rank-one connections. A connection with p-curvature zero is a Frobenius pullback of a line bundle (Cartier descent). Hence its point lies in A_s^{φ(p)} (=pE_s), the image of the Frobenius-pullback map. This gives question c): if ω(s) ∈ pE_s for all closed s, is the image of ω in A(S) torsion? Question b) asks: if moreover ω lies in the vector part V=Ker(E→A), is it zero?

On this page Grothendieck isolates from c) a question purely about abelian schemes.
(e) Let A/S be an abelian scheme and ω ∈ A(S). Suppose that for every closed point s, with p = char k(s), the point ω(s) lifts along the Verschiebung V: A_s^{(p)} → A_s to a k(s)-rational point. Must ω have finite order?

A crossed-out attempt starts: when S is (smooth?) dominant over Spec Z one has a map A^{(p/S)} → A, and considers the image of ω there. It is abandoned, and the page ends with 'fin 1ère partie'. The next page begins the second part: the linearized Cartier operator C̃: ω → ω^{(p)} on f_*Ω^1, its iterates F_*^{(ν)}, and the fixed-point identity F_*^{(ν)}ω = ω over F_{p^ν}.

Modern unpacking of (e): over a finite field k, Frobenius F: A(k) → A^{(p)}(k) is bijective on rational points, and V∘F = p. So the condition is exactly ω(s) ∈ p·A_s(k(s)) for every closed s, where p is the residue characteristic.
- When p does not divide #A_s(k(s)), the condition is vacuous.
- So it only bites at 'anomalous' closed points, where p | #A_s(k(s)).
- For an elliptic curve over Q with S = Spec Z[1/N], the condition reduces to: P ≡ O mod p at the anomalous primes with #E(F_p) = p.
errors: Not an error but a gap: the question is posed for all closed points of a fixed S. If S is allowed to shrink (almost all p), the condition becomes vacuous for 1-dimensional S whenever A has only finitely many anomalous primes. Whether a non-CM elliptic curve always has infinitely many is an open Lang–Trotter-type problem. So the answer to (e) is tied to unproven distribution statements, and (e) could fail as stated with shrinking.

The phrase 'la partie a) dans c) suggère' is loose. (e) is not a consequence or special case of c), since lifting along V in A is a different condition from lying in pE inside E. It is an analogue obtained by projecting to A.

ideas.what: Reformulating the rank-one p-curvature (Cartier fixed-point) problem as a question about sections of the universal vector extension E of the dual abelian scheme lying in pE_s (Frobenius-pullback locus) for all s
ideas.modern_name: Rank-one Grothendieck–Katz conjecture via the universal vector extension / moduli of rank-one connections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Katz conjecture (Katz 1972, attributing it to Grothendieck); rank-one case proved for curves by Chudnovsky and in general via Bost (2001) and André (2004) using algebraicity of leaves on commutative algebraic groups
ideas.where_published: Not by Grothendieck; the formulation appears in Katz's and André's work (unsure exactly where first)

ideas.what: Question (e): a section of an abelian scheme over S (finite type over Z) whose reduction at every closed point lies in the image of Verschiebung on rational points (equivalently in p·A_s(k(s))) — is it torsion?
ideas.modern_name: Local-global divisibility by the residue characteristic / detecting torsion by reductions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related themes: anomalous primes (Mazur 1972); detecting linear dependence by reduction (Kowalski, Pink, Gajda–Górnisiewicz and others); local-global divisibility (Dvornicich–Zannier, for fixed ℓ)
ideas.where_published: unsure; not aware of this exact formulation in print

ideas.what: Verschiebung V: A^{(p)} → A used as the 'dual' of Frobenius-descent condition on the group side

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses an arithmetic-geometric question: if a section of an abelian scheme over a Z-scheme lifts through Verschiebung (i.e. is p-divisible in A_s(k(s))) at every closed point, is it torsion? He abandons it at the end of the 'first part'.
missed.quote: e) Soit A schéma abélien sur S, ω section de A, telle que pour tout pt fermé s∈S, ω(s) se ramène à A_s^{(p)} via Verschiebung ... Est-il vrai qu'elle soit d'ordre fini ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Over 1-dimensional S the question is equivalent to a statement about reductions at anomalous primes, in Mazur's 1972 sense. With shrinking of S allowed, it is entangled with the open problem of the infinitude of anomalous primes. For higher-dimensional S (families) it might be accessible and seems not formulated in the literature. It is a 'point' analogue of the rank-one p-curvature conjecture, distinct from the Bost/André theorem.

missed.claim: The page implicitly links Grothendieck's p-curvature program (rank-one connections, Cartier fixed points) with the arithmetic of p-divisibility of points mod p, i.e. anomalous primes. The later literature (Mazur's Iwasawa-theoretic anomalous primes vs. Katz/Bost/André on p-curvature) developed these separately.
missed.quote: La partie a) dans c) suggère la question suivante
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests treating 'anomalous-prime' local conditions as a group-side shadow of vanishing p-curvature, a perspective not standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: The reduction of rank-one p-curvature to the universal vector extension is essentially known (Katz, André, Bost). However, the specific Verschiebung question (e) seems not to appear in print. It reduces to a nontrivial question about anomalous primes, which is a modestly interesting unpublished thread rather than a result.
transcription_corrections: The line read as '[?] (Ω^1 ...) = [?] fermé s∈S' should be 'pour tout pt fermé s∈S, ω(s) se ramène à A_s^{(p)} via'. The 'Ω^1' is a misreading of the handwriting.
The Verschiebung is 'A_s^{(p_s)} → A_s' (exponent the residue characteristic p_s), not '(p^n)'.
'Est-il vrai qu'elle [?] est d'ordre fini ?' should read 'Est-il vrai qu'elle soit d'ordre fini ?'.
Crossed-out block reads approximately: 'Dans le cas où S ... (par exemple ... dominant Spec Z) on dispose de A^{p/S} → A, et l'image ... de ω dans A^{p/S} est un ...'.

The faint left-margin and body text ('on suppose donc f_*(Ω^1_{X/S}) = f_*(Z^1_{X/S})...', 'NB au lieu de f_* on pourrait prendre R^i f_*', the C̃ computations) is show-through from the next page, not content of this page.
